Let
\[
s=aL,\qquad t=n^{-1/2}.
\]
We use
\[
S_1(N,a)=B(a,N+1)=\frac{\Gamma(a)\Gamma(N+1)}{\Gamma(N+a+1)}
\]
and
\[
S_2(N,a)=-\partial_a S_1(N,a)
=S_1(N,a)\bigl(\psi(N+a+1)-\psi(a)\bigr).
\]
Thus the determinant condition says that the two weighted averages of
\(\psi(N+a+1)\) are equal. Since \(\psi(N+a+1)=\log N+O(1/N)\), this becomes a weighted-average condition for \(\log N\), with errors smaller than the terms below.

For \(N=n^3+m_{j,n}\),
\[
N=n^3(1+jt+O(n^{-3})),\qquad u_j:=\log(1+jt).
\]
Also
\[
\frac{\Gamma(N+1)}{\Gamma(N+a+1)}
=N^{-a}\left(1-\frac{a(a+1)}{2N}+O(N^{-2})\right).
\]
Writing the determinant equation in terms of \(s=aL\), the only needed expansion near \(s=1\) is
\[
s-1=-\frac1{10}\frac{t^2}{L}+o\!\left(\frac{t^2}{L}\right).
\]
Here is the key coefficient computation. The chosen \(b_{j,n}\) satisfy
\[
\sum b_j=1,\qquad
\sum b_j j=\frac{12}{19},\qquad
\sum b_j j^2=-\frac{10}{19}t,
\]
so
\[
\sum b_j u_j=\frac{12}{19}t+O(t^3),
\qquad
\sum b_j u_j^2=\frac{8}{19}t^3+O(t^4).
\]
The finite-\(N\) correction from the \(S_1(n,a)\) denominator contributes
\[
\frac{a(a+1)}{2n}=\frac{t^2}{2L}+o\!\left(\frac{t^2}{L}\right).
\]
Combining these terms gives the determinant residual at \(s=1\):
\[
-\frac{6}{19}\frac{t^3}{L^2}+o\!\left(\frac{t^3}{L^2}\right),
\]
and its derivative with respect to \(s\):
\[
-\frac{60}{19}\frac{t}{L}+o\!\left(\frac{t}{L}\right).
\]
Therefore
\[
a_nL-1=s-1
=-\frac1{10}\frac{t^2}{L}+o\!\left(\frac{t^2}{L}\right).
\]
Since \(t=n^{-1/2}\),
\[
n^{3/2}L(a_nL-1)
=-\frac1{10}n^{1/2}+o(n^{1/2})\to -\infty.
\]

\[
\boxed{-\infty}
\]
